nodes.title: Your Name Under One Hour
nodes.summary: Major Lucius Carrington presses the quarrel at eleven round the master's empty chair and asks where your rounds took you; you tell the table you saw Nathaniel Yardley leave the back stairs at twenty to eleven and cross to the stables, and will swear to nothing else. Evangeline Davenport recites her eleven; Nathaniel kicks over his chair, bolts into the storm, is dragged back half-frozen and locked in. Millicent Gresham, tureen in hand, refuses you her hour.
nodes.image: Nathaniel's chair on its back, sleet rattling the black panes

nodes.title: The Hours Go to the Lawyer
nodes.summary: You walk the murder night again, one candle along the gallery, counting door to door: the quarrel at half past ten, one flame on the back stairs at eleven. Reginald Fairbrother never lifts his head. The roof's snow crashes past the windows and the Major comes out demanding your hours; you carry them past him to Cornelius Ellingham, who puts his name under yours and tells the Major they go to the magistrate, not before.
nodes.image: the roof's snow sliding past the gallery windows in one grey mass
who: the master's valet of forty years

nodes.title: Law's Name on the Gallery
nodes.summary: The eaves drip. Major Lucius Carrington bars you from the first floor and sends Lavinia Netherby to sift the study grate; you tell Cornelius Ellingham what you will say aloud if that grate is raked, and he climbs to the gallery and sends the maids down in law's name, naming his price after: the unsigned will never passes your lips. The Major posts Fairbrother at your door and walks Gideon Ashcombe across the slush to the ice house himself.
nodes.image: wet coal dripping from the hod on the landing, the sieve beside it
who: the master's valet of forty years
